correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact Exner–Tater square and hexagonal Floquet dispersion equations, expand the band-edge equations about k ell = m pi. For the square lattice the two edge displacements are odd to first order and their energy difference is 8/ell - 8 ell/(3 pi^2 m^2) + O(m^-4). For the hexagonal lattice the four relevant roots around the same flat-band point give total width 8(sqrt(3)-1)/ell + 8 ell(4-3 sqrt(3))/(3 pi^2 m^2) + O(m^-4). The absence of an m^-1 term makes the sums of local errors absolutely summable, so counting m <= ell sqrt(K)/pi gives the two stated finite-energy laws with O(1) remainders. A fresh independent numerical root solve at ell=0.7 and 1.4, m=60 and 120 made the residual after the displayed m^-2 correction scale as m^-4 with stable constants for both lattices.
residual_risks: The asymptotics concern the equilateral periodic lattices and the preferred-orientation coupling used by the source; other edge lengths or couplings are outside scope.
The O(1) remainder is not evaluated to a limiting constant.
